verdict_reason: Field-copy and deleted-derivation coverage is solid, but the camelCase test is a tautology against a self-configured ObjectMapper, the organisationId/status 'ignored' assertions are unfalsifiable because the body never carries those keys, and OperatorResponse's 11 null guards plus the optional-field path are wholly untested.

todos.issue: The camelCase 'contract lock' test builds its own ObjectMapper and sets LOWER_CAMEL_CASE + failOnUnknownProperties(false) itself, so it asserts the strategy the test just configured, not the production JacksonConfig — deleting JacksonConfig entirely leaves this test green; the assertions are also presence-only (json.has) so a field serialising as null still passes
todos.fix: Drop the hand-built mapper: either move this method into a @JsonTest/@SpringBootTest slice that injects the Spring-managed ObjectMapper (or applies JacksonConfig's Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer to a builder), and assert values not just key presence (json.get("addressLine1").asText() etc.); if the real-stack coverage in OperatorComplianceIT is deemed sufficient, delete this method rather than keep a tautology named as a contract lock

todos.issue: request_deserialisesFromCamelCaseAndMapsOntoAnEntityIgnoringServerFields asserts entity.getOrganisationId() and entity.getStatus() are null under the comment 'Server-assigned fields in the body are ignored', but the JSON body carries neither an organisationId nor a status key — only id and deleted — so both assertions are unfalsifiable; no test in the repo posts an organisationId in a body, leaving the cv-010 tenant-smuggling guard entirely unexercised
todos.fix: Add "organisationId": "OTHER-ORG", "status": "DELETED", "createdAt"/"modifiedAt" values to the body so the null assertions can actually fail, and add a matching AddressScopingIT case posting organisationId=ORG_B as ORG_A and asserting the persisted row is still ORG_A

todos.issue: sampleEntity always populates all 14 fields, so no test ever maps an entity with the genuinely optional addressLine2/county absent, and none of OperatorResponse's 11 Objects.requireNonNull guards (id, name, addressLine1, townOrCity, postcode, countryCode, phone, email, organisationId, createdAt, modifiedAt) is exercised — a repo-wide grep for requireNonNull/NullPointerException/assertThatThrownBy/assertThrows in src/test returns nothing, so the deliberate fail-loud behaviour on a legacy or partially-written Mongo row is unpinned
todos.fix: Add two cases: toResponse on an entity with null addressLine2 and null county maps cleanly (guards stay off the optional fields), and assertThatThrownBy(() -> operatorMapper.toResponse(entityWithNullPhone)).isInstanceOf(NullPointerException.class).hasMessage("phone") to pin at least one required-field guard
